title: Prove native payload dimension for owner-local centre repairs
body:
PR2461 proves a sharp 104-coordinate owner-local repair floor on constant payloads and leaves general native operator rank open. For the same selected calls 0/4, this package proves the conditional full-payload floor 104*d, where d is the complete payload dimension. It audits both 24,767-event local orientations on all 704 ordinary formal columns, verifies 2,896 used native recipes on all 512 columns and all 112 completed source-to-target blocks, and finds the backward queries use only T, with coefficients R/4. The 112 distinct owner routes then give a direct-sum rank 112*d against old transcript rank 8*d, with a sharp abstract 104-array reconstruction.

The global interpretation explicitly assumes invertible full-space row views on equal finite payload spaces; the 73-axis physical compiler is not rebuilt. The local 512-dimensional factor is not treated as the entire physical payload. This is an information bound for linear owner-local encoders with arbitrary cross-owner decoding and recovery of every later internal query. It supplies no native repair, physical access/restoration/hosting invoice, recursive-child lower bound, precision proof, new supplier or exponent.

Validation: the native CPython 3.12.7 registered suite passes the optimized primary and all six Git-free/source-corruption/typed-receipt checks. Seven semantic controls include a constant-preserving singular map that exposes why scalar evidence alone is insufficient. A separate OpenAI Codex reviewer reran the primary under native 3.14.5, independently extracted all 16 query rows by reverse-adjoint replay from the raw archive, checked different three-coordinate payload maps with ranks 24/336/336/335, and found no material issue within the explicit conditional contract. No human review or formal verification is claimed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-native-observation-dimension`.

PR2461's scalar/route checker, PR2048's exact operator helpers, PR2391's native counterexample, the selected construction and Lemma G/Clifford lineage are pinned and credited. The existing claim is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2461#issuecomment-6195603044. Canonical main was refreshed before submission; exact overlap limitations and open physical-repair/final-output questions are retained. Prepared for ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
